fullparsedJSON.title: Minuscule P-partition cyclic sieving conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $P$ be a minuscule poset, let $r(P)$ denote its rank, and set $h=r(P)+2$. For $\ell\geq 1$, let $\mathrm{PP}^{\ell}(P)$ be the $P$-partitions of height $\ell$, let $\mathrm{row}$ be piecewise-linear rowmotion, and define

$$
F(P,\ell)=\prod_{p\in P}\frac{1-q^{r(p)+\ell+1}}{1-q^{r(p)+1}}.
$$

**Minuscule P-partition cyclic sieving conjecture.** For every $\ell\geq 1$, the triple

$$
(\mathrm{PP}^{\ell}(P),\langle\mathrm{row}\rangle,F(P,\ell))
$$

exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.

This extends the known order-$\ell=1$ result of Rush and Shi and is known for rectangles by work of Rhoades. The conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Sam Hopkins, “Minuscule doppelgängers, the coincidental down-degree expectations property, and rowmotion”, arXiv:1902.07301 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.07301

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2019). “In this paper, we do not resolve this final conjecture of Reiner-Tenner-Yong, but we do situate it in what we believe is the correct context, and suggest a program which could resolve it.”

fullparsedJSON.title: The self-conjugate consecutive-core and symmetric generalized Dyck path conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $s$ and $k$ be positive integers. A **self-conjugate $(s,s+1,\dots,s+k)$-core** is a self-conjugate partition that is simultaneously an $s$-core, $(s+1)$-core, and so on through an $(s+k)$-core. A **symmetric $(s,k)$-generalized Dyck path** is a generalized Dyck path with parameters $(s,k)$ that is invariant under the relevant reflection symmetry. **Self-conjugate consecutive-core conjecture.** The number of self-conjugate $(s,s+1,\dots,s+k)$-cores is equal to the number of symmetric $(s,k)$-generalized Dyck paths. This extends the proved case of three consecutive core parameters established earlier in the paper; the conjecture proposes the corresponding equality for every pair of positive integers $s$ and $k$.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Hyunsoo Cho, JiSun Huh and Jaebum Sohn, “Counting self-conjugate (s,s+1,s+2)-core partitions”, arXiv:1904.02313 (2019).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.02313

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: The sticky polymatroid conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $h$ be a polymatroid, and call it **sticky** if any two extensions of $h$ have an amalgam. A polymatroid is **modular** when its rank function satisfies the modularity condition for every pair of subsets.

**Sticky polymatroid conjecture.** Every sticky polymatroid is modular.

The statement extends the sticky matroid conjecture from matroids to polymatroids. The source gives no resolution or evidence establishing its status.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Laszlo Csirmaz, “One-adhesive polymatroids”, arXiv:1904.07565 (2019).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07565

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: The square-free positivity conjecture for equivariant matroid K-classes
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements with $e$ connected components. Write its equivariant K-class in terms of double Grothendieck polynomials:

$$
\mathcal{K}(M)=\sum_{\lambda:\,\lambda_1\leq n-r}c_\lambda(t)\mathfrak{S}_\lambda(u,t).
$$

**Square-free positivity conjecture.** The Laurent polynomials $(-1)^{r(n-r)-(n-e)-|\lambda|}c_\lambda(t)\in\mathbf{Z}[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_n^{\pm1}]$ can be expressed, non-uniquely, as square-free polynomials in the quantities $t_j/t_i-1$, for $1\leq i<j\leq n$, with positive integer coefficients.

This conjecture strengthens the previously known positivity statement for realizable matroids and is motivated by analogous positivity for K-theoretic Littlewood–Richardson coefficients. Its general validity for all matroids remains open.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Andrew Berget and Alex Fink, “Equivariant K-theory classes of matrix orbit closures”, arXiv:1904.10047 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: The square-free positivity conjecture for equivariant matroid Chow classes
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $r$ on $n$ elements with $e$ connected components. Write its equivariant Chow class in terms of double Schur polynomials:

$$
\mathcal{C}(M)=\sum_{\lambda:\,\lambda_1\leq n-r}d_\lambda(t)s_\lambda(u,t).
$$

**Chow square-free positivity conjecture.** The polynomial $(-1)^{r(n-r)-(n-e)-|\lambda|}d_\lambda(t)\in\mathbf{Z}[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ can be expressed, non-uniquely, as a square-free polynomial in the quantities $t_i-t_j$, for $1\leq i<j\leq n$, with non-negative integer coefficients.

This is the Chow-theoretic consequence of the equivariant K-theory positivity conjecture. A weaker positivity result is known for matroids realizable over $\mathbf{C}$, while the assertion for arbitrary matroids remains open.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Andrew Berget and Alex Fink, “Equivariant K-theory classes of matrix orbit closures”, arXiv:1904.10047 (2021).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: The discrete-excess conjecture for the contradictory component in random 2-SAT
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $F$ be chosen uniformly at random from the set $\mathcal F(n,m)$ of 2-CNF formulas, and let $\xi$ denote the total excess of the strongly connected contradictory component in the corresponding random implication digraph. The parameter $\mu$ is defined by $m=n(1+\mu n^{-1/3})$. **Discrete-excess conjecture.** If $\mu$ is constant, the distribution of $\xi$ is discrete. Moreover, when $\mu$ is constant, the number of strongly connected components of the contradictory-component digraph has a discrete limiting law; when $\mu\to+\infty$, the contradictory component is strongly connected with high probability. The conjecture describes the discrete structure expected at the critical 2-SAT phase transition; the paper notes simulation-based evidence, but no proof or resolution is supplied.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Sergey Dovgal, “The birth of the contradictory component in random 2-SAT”, arXiv:1904.10266 (2019).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.10266

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: Two-line intersection conjecture for rich-line-free point sets
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a finite point set. For a line $l$, let $L(P)\cap l$ denote the set of points where lines from $L(P)$ intersect $l$. Assume that no more than $|P|^{1-\delta}$ points of $P$ lie on any line, and let $l_1$ and $l_2$ be distinct arbitrary lines. For every $\delta>0$ there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(\delta)>0$ such that

$$
|L(P)\cap l_1|+|L(P)\cap l_2|\gg |P|^{1+\epsilon}.
$$

**Two-line intersection conjecture.** For all $\delta>0$, there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(\delta)>0$ for which the displayed bound holds for every such $P$, $l_1$, and $l_2$. This conjecture predicts a sum-product-type expansion for intersections of the line set with two distinct lines, once very rich lines in $P$ are excluded; its status is open in the supplied source.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Oliver Roche-Newton and Audie Warren, “New Expander Bounds from Affine Group Energy”, arXiv:1905.03701 (2019).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.03701

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: Cichacz–Froncek conjecture on distance magic graphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **distance magic labeling** of $G$ is a bijection from its vertices to the cyclic group of order $|V(G)|$ for which every vertex has the same neighbor-sum. A graph is **group distance magic** if it admits a $\Gamma$-distance magic labeling for every Abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $|V(G)|$.

**Cichacz–Froncek conjecture.** If $G$ is a distance magic graph, then $G$ is group distance magic.

The conjecture asks whether existence of a distance magic labeling with the cyclic group always implies existence of such a labeling for every Abelian group of the same order. The source presents this as an open conjecture and notes that many distance magic graphs are already known to be group distance magic.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Sylwia Cichacz, Dalibor Froncek and Paweł Dyrlaga, “Group distance magic Cartesian product of two cycles”, arXiv:1905.04946 (2019).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.04946

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: Period invariance of the graph-theoretic $c_2$-invariant
fullparsedJSON.statement:
For primitive graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$, let $P(G_i)$ denote their periods and let $c_2^{(q)}(G_i)$ denote the reduction modulo $q$ of the graph point-count divided by $q^2$. **Period-invariance conjecture.** If $P(G_1)=P(G_2)$, then

$$
c_2^{(q)}(G_1)\equiv c_2^{(q)}(G_2)\mod q
$$

for all prime powers $q$. This conjecture expresses the expectation that the $c_2$-invariant detects information intrinsic to the period; it holds in all presently known examples.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Oliver Schnetz, “Geometries in perturbative quantum field theory”, arXiv:1905.08083 (2023).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08083

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2019). “Although the conjecture is false in general , a connection between the point-counting function and the period $()$ remains valid.”

fullparsedJSON.title: Neguț's positivity conjecture for generalized $q,t$-Catalan polynomials
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $a_1\geqslant a_2\geqslant \cdots\geqslant a_n\geqslant 0$, and let $f(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ be the polynomial in $q$ and $t$ defined in the paper.

**Neguț's conjecture.** The polynomial $f(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ has nonnegative coefficients.

This conjecture generalizes the coefficient positivity of rational and ordinary $q,t$-Catalan numbers to arbitrary weakly decreasing sequences. It is proved in the paper for the cases covered by its results, but remains open in general.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Eugene Gorsky, Graham Hawkes, Anne Schilling and Julianne Rainbolt, “Generalized q,t-Catalan numbers”, arXiv:1905.10973 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.10973

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2019).

fullparsedJSON.title: The crystalline kernel conjecture for Delone sets
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $X\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a Delone set with parameter $R$. For each point $x\in X$, let $S_x(2R)$ be its local group, and let $K$ be the subset of points whose local groups contain axes only of orders $2$, $3$, $4$, or $6$. **Crystalline kernel conjecture.** The crystalline kernel $K$ is a Delone subset with some parameter $R'\leq kR$, where $k$ is a constant independent of $X$. This conjecture asserts that the points with only crystallographic rotational orders remain uniformly relatively dense; the source gives no resolution of the claim.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Nikolay Dolbilin, “Local Groups in Delone Sets”, arXiv:2011.00558 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.00558

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Projection formulation of the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement:
For $A\subset\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$ and $r\in\mathbb{Q}\cup\\{\infty\\}$, define

$$
\pi_r(A)=\\{x+ry:(x,y)\in A\\},
$$

with $x+\infty y=y$. **Projection formulation of the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, there exist $r_1,\ldots,r_k\in\mathbb{Q}\cup\\{\infty\\}$, none equal to $-1$, such that for every $A\subset\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$,

$$
|\pi_{-1}(A)|\leq\max_{i=1,\ldots,k}|\pi_{r_i}(A)|^{1+\epsilon}.
$$

The source presents this as another equivalent formulation of the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Charlie Cowen-Breen, Elene Karangozishvili, Narmada Varadarajan and Thomas Wang, “Pattern Problems related to the Arithmetic Kakeya Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.07056 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.07056

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The unlabelled weighted graph conjecture for horizontal-strip LLT polynomials
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $\bm\lambda$ and $\bm\mu$ be horizontal strips, and let $\Pi(\bm\lambda)$ and $\Pi(\bm\mu)$ be their weighted graphs. If

$$
\Pi(\bm\lambda)\cong\Pi(\bm\mu)
$$

as weighted graphs, then the associated LLT polynomials satisfy

$$
G_{\bm\lambda}(\bm x;q)=G_{\bm\mu}(\bm x;q).
$$

This conjecture extends the triangle-free result to arbitrary weighted graphs arising from horizontal strips: the LLT polynomial should be determined by the unlabelled weighted graph. No resolution is supplied in the source.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Foster Tom, “A combinatorial Schur expansion of triangle-free horizontal-strip LLT polynomials”, arXiv:2011.13671 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.13671

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: The IU-family weighted-sum conjecture
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and let an **IU-family** be a family $\mathcal F\subset 2^{[n]}$ such that for every $F,G\in\mathcal F$, one has $F\cap G\neq\emptyset$ and $F\cup G\neq[n]$. **IU-family weighted-sum conjecture.** One should have

$$
\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\frac{1}{{n\choose |F|}}\leq\frac{n+1}{6}.
$$

The bound improves the general estimate $\frac{\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lceil n/2\rceil}{n}\leq n/4$ obtained from Katona's circle method. The source presents the denominator $6$ as conjectural, and no resolution is supplied.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Peter Frankl, “Old and new applications of Katona's circle”, arXiv:2011.14252 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14252

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Multiplicity-freeness conjecture for antipodes of Hopf-class monoids
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $\textbf{\textsc{pre}}^\natural$ denote the Hopf monoid arising from a Hopf class; equivalently, consider every Hopf monoid arising from a Hopf class. **Multiplicity-freeness conjecture.** In every Hopf monoid arising from a Hopf class (equivalently, in $\textbf{\textsc{pre}}^\natural$), the antipode is multiplicity-free. This is a broader formulation of the paper's antipode multiplicity-freeness question. The paper obtains such formulas for particular Hopf monoids, but the assertion for every Hopf monoid arising from a Hopf class remains open.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Federico Castillo, Jeremy L. Martin and Jose A. Samper, “Hopf monoids of ordered simplicial complexes”, arXiv:2011.14955 (2024).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14955

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2020). “It was proven in that every generic real-valued function on the ground set of a matroid, when extended linearly to bases, gives rise to a shelling order on the independence complex.”

fullparsedJSON.title: Polytopality conjecture for the oriented graph of a positive braid
fullparsedJSON.statement: Let $\beta$ be an arbitrary positive braid word, and let $D_\beta$ be the oriented graph obtained from $\beta$ by including edges for $ss\to s$, $s_i s_{i+1}s_i\to s_{i+1}s_i s_{i+1}$, and $s_i s_j\to s_j s_i$ for $|i-j|\geq2$, then contracting all edges of the last type. The resulting graph defines a poset, and its poset complex is the associated simplicial complex. **Polytopality conjecture.** The poset complex of $D_\beta$ is either a sphere or a ball. If it is a sphere, it admits a polytopal realization. This expectation links the weave combinatorics to higher Bruhat orders and to the ball-or-sphere and polytopality phenomena for subword complexes.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Roger Casals, Eugene Gorsky, Mikhail Gorsky and José Simental, “Algebraic Weaves and Braid Varieties”, arXiv:2012.06931 (2024).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.06931

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Finite-support conjecture for clique-density optimizers
fullparsedJSON.statement:
For $2\leq i\leq k$, let $a_i$ be coefficients and define a graph parameter by 
$$
\lambda(G):=\sum_{i=2}^k a_i p(K_i,G),
$$
 where $p(K_i,G)$ is the induced density of the clique $K_i$. Let $OPT$ denote the set of optimal vectors, and let $\mathbold{x}$ be such a vector. **Finite-support conjecture.** For every $\lambda(G):=\sum_{i=2}^k a_i p(K_i,G)$, every $\mathbold{x}\in OPT$ has finite support. This is stated as an open question in the paper; the supplied context gives no resolution.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Hong Liu, Oleg Pikhurko, Maryam Sharifzadeh and Katherine Staden, “Stability from graph symmetrisation arguments with applications to inducibility”, arXiv:2012.10731 (2023).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.10731

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Cohen–Perkins–Sarantis–Tetali conjecture for independent sets in linear hypergraphs
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $H=(V,E)$ be a $d$-regular, $k$-uniform, linear hypergraph on $n$ vertices, and let $i(H)$ denote its number of independent sets. Here, $d$-regular means that every vertex lies in $d$ edges, $k$-uniform means that every edge has $k$ vertices, and linear means that any two distinct edges share at most one vertex.

**Cohen–Perkins–Sarantis–Tetali conjecture.** For every such hypergraph,

$$
\frac{\log_2 i(H)}{n}\leqslant \frac{k-1}{k}+\frac{\log_2 k}{kd}.
$$

The conjecture is intended to sharpen the general container-method upper bound by improving its second-order term. The source presents it as an open conjecture; no proof or disproof is given there.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Aliaksei Semchankau, Dmitry Shabanov and Ilya Shkredov, “Number of A+BC solutions in abelian groups and application to counting independent sets in hypergraphs”, arXiv:2012.13433 (2020).
fullparsedJSON.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.13433

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

fullparsedJSON.title: Negative correlation conjecture for uniformly random spanning forests
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $\mathbf{F}$ be a uniformly random forest chosen from all forests of $G$. For edges $e,f\in E(G)$, **negative correlation conjecture.**

$$
\mathbb{P}(e,f\in \mathbf{F})\leq \mathbb{P}(e\in \mathbf{F})\mathbb{P}(f\in \mathbf{F}).
$$

This conjecture asks whether edge inclusion events are negatively correlated for a uniformly random spanning forest. The source describes it as a well-known open problem and notes that it implies the regular-graph spanning-forest bound above.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Ferenc Bencs and Péter Csikvári, “Upper bound for the number of spanning forests of regular graphs”, arXiv:2105.06801 (2022).
fullparsedJSON.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2005.12752](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12752).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.06801

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

fullparsedJSON.title: Frankl's conjecture for even $n+t$ and $t$-intersecting $k$-Sperner families
fullparsedJSON.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$. The family $\mathcal{F}$ is **$t$-intersecting** if $|A\cap B|\geq t$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal{F}$, and it is **$k$-Sperner** if it contains no chain of length $k+1$. Suppose that $n+t$ is even and $n>t$. **Frankl's conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}$ is a $t$-intersecting $k$-Sperner family, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leq \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}\binom{n}{(n+t)/2+i}.
$$

The conjectured extremal construction consists of the $k$ consecutive layers beginning at level $(n+t)/2$. Frankl proved the conjecture in several ranges; the general common extension of Milner's and Frankl's theorems remains open.
fullparsedJSON.source_name: Jia-Bao Yang and Leilei Zhang, “Counterexamples to the Balogh-Linz-Patkós Conjecture”, arXiv:2607.03026 (2026).
fullparsedJSON.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2209.01656](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.01656), [arXiv:2008.08792](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08792).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.03026

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).
